description: Heritage escape-spelling diagnostic identity is CANONICAL, not the surface spelling (issue #737). With Heritage active, `output 5` and `op 6` at top level are outside any procedure and are caught by the semantic checker's control-flow rule (`checker-control-flow.ts`). `output`/`op` are Heritage *alternate spellings* of Core `return` (`spec/conformance.md#heritage` — "alternate spellings only, no new semantics"), lowered onto the same `Return` node, so all three spellings are ONE condition and must carry ONE machine-readable identity: `params.keyword` is `"return"` for both lines here — byte-identical to the two diagnostics `return 5` / `return 6` raises (`tests/conformance/core-language/check/return-outside-proc` is the single-line Core twin). Diagnostic identity is `code` plus structured `params` and the same condition MUST keep the same params (`spec/error-model.md:235-238`); a param whose value changed with the spelling would be an observable semantic difference. The prose `message` DOES name the learner's own word (`output …`, `op …`) — that is the localization boundary and is permitted — and `source_span` still covers exactly the surface control word (6 columns for `output`, 2 for `op`), proving canonicalizing the param did not canonicalize the span. This fixture asserts `params.keyword` directly: the absence of such an assertion is what let all three instances of this bug class ship.

diagnostics.message: output only reports a value from inside a procedure. put it between 'define' and 'end'.
op only reports a value from inside a procedure. put it between 'define' and 'end'.
